notes.title: Mini-demo of Weapon Customization in Status Entropos & FAQ
notes.content:
[p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45344753/78abcf3aa47822a3b03a988649a077c5f77ce5c1.jpg"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45344753/f0a3319cacde0645601a4cdf4b4031df9f58ea2c.jpg"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45344753/2dc0018476f6dfb687fe2fe096d91e8b28f0b966.jpg"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45344753/4c4b3adec5990b3e105dc78e28f25978fefcc8e9.jpg"][/img][/p][p][b]Q: What attachments will be customizable?[/b]
A: In the first versions of weapon customization, you’ll be able to change sights, magazines, and camouflages. The system will gradually expand.

[b]Q: Will there be deep customization like in Escape from Tarkov, Ground Branch, Deadline, etc.?[/b]
A: That’s our plan. First, we’ll focus on full functional customization, what matters for gameplay, and in the future, we’ll try to implement advanced options more for aesthetics.

[b]Q: Will it be possible to install 2 (3, 5, 10) sights at once?[/b]
A: If you install a sight, the other sight slots will be locked. But you’ll be able to add a magnifier to some collimators/holographs, or an extra canted sight to certain optics.

[b]Q: Will there be a system for saving different builds of the same weapon?[/b]
A: Yes, you’ll be able to save up to 10 builds for each weapon. We also plan to add the ability to share your builds with other players in the future.

[b]Q: Is it possible to “ruin” a weapon’s stats with “bad” customization?[/b]
A: Not really — you’ll be able to install modules that don’t fit your playstyle, but you won’t be able to make a weapon fully unusable.

[b]Q: Are there any class/type restrictions for customization?[/b]
A: Yes. For example, you can’t put a bipod, optics or a drum mag on an AKS-74U — every weapon has its own intended use. We approach customization not as a theoretical “workshop build” but rather with practical justification for each module on each weapon.

[b]Q: Can you test your builds on the range before going into battle?[/b]
A: Yes. I put a lot of effort on UX and Quality-of-Life in Status Entropos: you’ll be able to view available attachments and test every weapon on the shooting range even before you buy it. The customization menu itself will have handy features for checking your build — different view modes, aiming mode, and instant access to the range.

Also I've made a big post about customization on Patreon, with UI screenshots and other images and a short video: 
[url="https://www.patreon.com/posts/early-concepts-133819289"]https://www.patreon.com/posts/early-concepts-133819289[/url][/p][p][/p][p][i]— Max Ulman & the June Folks team[/i][/p]

notes.title: The time has come
notes.content:
Troopers, attention!

Entropia is entering Pre-Alpha and launching its first demo!
After months of work, we're ready to share the first results. This is just the beginning — with your support, we’ll keep pushing forward according to our roadmap: https://entropiathegame.com/en/roadmap

[previewyoutube=UWAb4klE_so;full][/previewyoutube]

[h2]What’s Included in Pre-Alpha[/h2]
[h3]Tech demo[/h3]
Before we begin crowdfunding for further development, we want to show that the game exists and already has a technical foundation.

Our goal is to build a proper tactical shooter with satisfying gunplay and deep weapon mechanics. Over the past year, we’ve built the groundwork for an animation system that blends procedural and traditional animations, developed an in-depth destruction system based on Chaos engine, laid the foundation for our visual style, and shaped the gameplay concept we’re aiming for.

In the current version, you’ll be able to test out weapons and destruction, check out the class-based characters — and even play against each other!

[h3]Playtests[/h3]
We’ll be running periodic playtest sessions in the 4v4 Skirmish mode — a small-scale mode for fast-paced firefights on compact maps. Once we can move to dedicated servers, we’ll roll out the full-scale game modes: Raid and **Combat.
The shooting range will always be available offline. Later on, we plan to let you invite friends to the range as well.

[h3]When?[/h3]
The first wave of access will launch this week for players who support Entropia on Patreon!

Pre-Alpha Trailer: https://youtu.be/UWAb4klE_so
Patreon: https://www.patreon.com/c/junefolks
Boosty: https://boosty.to/entropiathegame

notes.title: FAQ #2
notes.content:
[i]Greetings, troopers! Since more and more people are discovering the game, I’ll take a moment to answer some of the most frequently asked questions[/i]

[i]The first FAQ can be found here: https://discord.com/channels/1168965393109500064/1170866189807931522/1320128463524462623[/i]

[b]Q: What games can Entropia be compared to? Battlefield, Escape from Tarkov, Counter-Strike?[/b]
A: The simplest comparison would be “Insurgency: Sandstorm with destruction.” We’re aiming for a simcade formula—blending deep, realistic mechanics with accessible and engaging gameplay.

The core game modes focus on attack and defense in CQB, cover-based combat, destruction, special gadgets, and teamwork. That said, from the start, there will be a small Skirmish mode for those who prefer fast-paced and simple gameplay. In the future, we also plan to introduce a large-scale 40-player mode, reminiscent of Battlefield’s Breakthrough mode.

[b]Q: When can we expect the Pre-Alpha, and what are you working on right now?[/b]
A: Right now, we’re working on two CQB maps, visual effects, polishing animation systems, making the Pre-Alpha trailer, and fixing minor bugs. We expect the Pre-Alpha launch by the end of this month.

[b]Q: What will the Pre-Alpha version of the game include?[/b]
A: The Pre-Alpha is a very small tech demo. At this stage, the goal is to showcase the core ideas of the game, gather feedback, and kickstart additional funding through crowdfunding to expand the team and develop a solid Alpha version by the end of the year.

The game will be available in both offline (shooting range) and online (PvP) modes:
- The offline shooting range will always be accessible. You’ll be able to try out weapons, controls, and the destruction system.
- Online sessions will be hosted every 1-2 weeks.

[b]Q: What is the Skirmish mode?[/b]
A: Skirmish is one of the four planned game modes in Entropia. It’s a small-scale CQB mode for 8 players, where two teams of 4 players fight under classic Team Deathmatch rules.

Originally, this mode was meant for a later stage of development, as a supplement to the two main modes—Combat and Raid. However, during internal testing, we ran into session hosting issues on our personal PCs, since we don’t have dedicated servers yet. Since we currently can’t reliably host large-scale sessions, we decided to start with this fast-paced close-quarters mode and gradually expand into the larger tactical modes.

[b]Q: Will there be mod support?[/b]
A: We have huge respect for modders, but full modding support is unlikely in Entropia. We might consider limited modding possibilities after the full launch. Also, one of our long-term goals is to introduce a flexible game mode editor for custom servers.

[b]Q: Will there be bots or an offline mode?[/b]
A: Bots won’t be added to online sessions. However, after the full launch, we might consider a training/offline mode with bots if we have enough resources to develop AI.

[b]Q: Will weapon sounds be improved?[/b]
A: Yes! As soon as we can, we’ll completely revamp all sound effects and plan to transition to the Wwise audio engine, which will allow for realistic positioning and reverb effects for indoor firefights.

[h2]Brief recap of previously answered questions[/h2]

[b]Q: What platforms?[/b]
A: PC only.

[b]Q: Gamepad support?[/b]
A: Maybe. Not a priority.

[b]Q: Paid game?[/b]
A: Yes.

[b]Q: Microtransactions?[/b]
A: Minimal. Authentic camouflages for gear and weapons.

[b]Q: Drivable vehicles?[/b]
A: Planned for larger game modes.

[b]Q: Why do walls break that easy?[/b]
A: Testing the destruction system. Won’t be like this in the game.

[b]Q: Will weapon N be in the game?[/b]
A: High chance, our roadmap includes 100+ weapons.

Thank you for your interest in Entropia!
If you have additional questions, suggestions, or just want to discuss the game, feel free to leave a comment in chat.
Stay in touch!

notes.title: Shooting & Destruction — Work in Progress
Recker — Updated Character Model
notes.content:
As we mentioned in [url=https://entropiathegame.com/en/news/5]January News Summary[/url], we’re currently refining character models. Today, we’re sharing screenshots of the updated model for the American Assaulter — Recker.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45344753/142c4f5fcd45f6b35c056b14875ee50cc6d758d3.png[/img]

[h3]What’s Been Done[/h3]
- The model has been almost entirely reworked: body proportions have been corrected, and the gear is now bulkier and more realistically baggy. No more "scrawny" characters, as one of our testers put it! :)
- All equipment has been adjusted and fitted to match real-world counterparts: the body armor, its cummerbunds and pouches, the drop pouch, footwear, patches, and other details.
- The entire character model is now designed with future modular customization in mind, ensuring proper separation into individual parts when the time comes.
- Textures have been revised and enhanced: colors adjusted, camouflage stylization refined, detail increased (stitching is now visible on fabric), and overall resolution improved.

Interestingly, despite all these improvements, we’ve managed to optimize the polygon count by approximately 10%—experience pays off!

Of course, this isn’t the only thing we’ve worked on this week. In parallel, we’re enhancing the destruction system, refining parkour mechanics, finalizing gunplay, composing soundtracks, and preparing for the trailer shoot—each handled by different team members, bringing us closer to the Pre-Alpha release. Next week, we’ll be sharing updates on some of these as well!

What do you think of the updated Recker? Share your thoughts!

notes.title: Class system in Entropia
notes.content:
Hey, gamers! In today’s post, I want to tell you about the class system in Entropia and why we’ve chosen to include it in our game.

[h2]Why a class system?[/h2]

[img]https://static.tildacdn.net/tild6361-3564-4066-b363-346366336666/Ronny_blue.jpg[/img]

Before development began, when we were just sketching out the game’s design document, we didn’t have anything concrete in front of us—only a vision of the experience and emotions the game should deliver. At the core of it all was the player: their comfort and freedom (both tactically and generally). Alongside this, we’d always envisioned a progression system. After all, to avoid overwhelming new players with too many mechanics and content right off the bat, there had to be a way to ease them into the game while also providing a sense of growth and achievement—unlocking new levels, weapons, gadgets, sights, or suppressors.

Even without an RPG system (meaning no leveling up health or movement speed), more experienced players naturally have greater tactical options than newcomers. Even with equal skill, the ”veteran” has an advantage thanks to those new weapons and mechanics, plus knowledge of maps and mechanics. This needed a solution!

That’s where the class system came: pre-defined, specialized roles with ready-to-go modified weapons, special gadgets, grenades, and unique attributes. When a new player joins the game, they immediately have access to five roles tailored to different playstyles. From the start, players have all the basic tools they need to handle most situations, making skill—not grinding—the deciding factor in battles.

[h3]What classes will be available?[/h3]

Entropia features five base classes, each relatively standard in their design:

- [b]Assaulter[/b]. A versatile attack specialist: assault rifles, explosives, and sledgehammers—everything needed to breach enemy fortifications.
- [b]Heavy gunner[/b]. A defensive specialist: heavy armor, machine guns, and heavy battle rifles.
- [b]Medic[/b]. A mobile support specialist with advanced medical skills. Despite lighter armor, he remains dangerous in close combat.
- [b]Techman[/b]. An expert in electronics and technology, fortifications, demolitions, and traps.
- [b]Recon[/b]. A specialist in enemy detection, precision eliminations, and sabotage.

We recently updated the section on classes on our website, where you can check out how these characters look: [url=https://entropiathegame.com/en/wiki/classes]https://entropiathegame.com/en/wiki/classes[/url]

But that’s not all. As you progress through the game, you’ll unlock subclasses—three specializations for each character, making a total of 15 unique roles. For instance, the [b]Recon[/b] class starts as a [b]Sniper[/b] but also can branch out into a [b]Marksman[/b] or a [b]Saboteur[/b]. Completely different tasks and tactical possibilities—and no tedious grinding or hours of character tweaking!

[h2]Your character[/h2]

Classes aren’t just for newcomer, nor are they something that limits you. Think of them as balanced, pre-built kits for different combat scenarios and playstyles. But if you love fine-tuning every detail of your character, you’ll have that opportunity too!

We haven’t talked about the sixth class yet, which unlocks after a brief introduction to the game’s mechanics. The [b]Trooper[/b] is a special class with flexible weapon and equipment choices, as well as visual customization. It’s not a universal soldier, it doesn’t overshadow the strengths of standard classes, it’s [b]your[/b] character narrow focused to your unique playstyle.

If you enjoy diving into every detail of your loadout, you’ll be able to customize:

- Primary weapon
- Secondary weapon
- Light and heavy equipment (gadgets and special tools)
- Grenades
- Melee weapons
- Supplies and consumables like medkits or additional armor plates
- Special skills, perks, or upgrades
- Body armor
- Flaps with different ammo

We’re also planning an extensive system for customizing your character’s appearance: faces, voices, gear, and more. While we’re not ready to reveal details just yet (since gameplay mechanics take priority), we aim to create a flexible system befitting a modern tactical shooter with a strong focus on equipment and atmosphere.

[h2]Character is a story[/h2]

Beyond their gameplay roles, each character in Entropia has a deep personal story that reflects not only their development but also the upheavals of the Entropia lore. Over time, we’ll shed light on different characters and events.

Both in gameplay and as part of the whole project, our goal is to create a living world with characters you can believe in, empathize with, or despise. After all, we play games for the emotions they evoke.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45344753/0af54a82e3ba153ec3465657e7612268bd85e62c.jpg[/img]

[h2]Quick Q&A about the class system:[/h2]

[b]Q: Will classes be limited per team?[/b]
A: No, we plan to let players pick whichever character they want without restrictions. If you have a specific strategy in mind, why limit it?

[b]Q: Will there be an inventory system like in Escape from Tarkov or S.T.A.L.K.E.R.? Can we pick up weapons from dead enemies?[/b]
A: You’ll be able to pick up weapons and other items from dead enemies or allies if you have the appropriate slot. The inventory system is similar to Insurgency. However, to avoid piles of weapons and grenades dropping from every corpse, we’re designing a convenient mini-interface for more streamlined looting.

[b]Q: Will class characters have different health, armor, or ammo amounts?[/b]
A: All characters have the same health. However, armor and ammo amounts depend on their equipment—naturally, combat-focused classes will have heavier armor and more ammunition than support roles.

[b]Q: Can class characters be customized?[/b]
A: Yes, there will be some customization options, though not as extensive as with the Trooper class.

[b]Q: Will we be able to create and save multiple loadouts for our custom class?[/b]
A: Similar to the specializations of standard classes, you’ll be able to prepare and save multiple setups for your custom character.

Thanks for reading, and stay tuned!
[i]— Max Ulman and the June Folks team[/i]

notes.title: FAQ #1
notes.content:
[i]Greetings! Max Ulman here, and I’ve prepared answers to the most frequently asked questions.[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45344753/6397cd9d590f684ec134084c7ce99876393c2502.jpg[/img]

[h2]Q: What will the gameplay be like? Will it resemble Squad, Insurgency, Escape from Tarkov, Call of Duty, etc.?[/h2]
A: We're aiming to create brutal, immersive gameplay focused on close-quarters combat, cover mechanics, attack and defense. Features like low TTK, surface penetration and destruction, the ability to build your own cover, suppression and panic effects, and authentic, uncensored voice lines are designed to deliver intense and thrilling emotions—that’s our priority!
We’re not chasing pure simulation or maximum realism. Instead, we’re paying attention to plausibility, justification, and the military aesthetic.
To give you a better idea of what to expect, you might describe Entropia as a mix of Insurgency’s grit and grounded realism, Rainbow Six: Siege’s tactical depth, and a touch of Battlefield’s "Breakthrough" mode.

[h2]Q: Why does the graphics look so rough?[/h2]
A: Graphics are typically polished in the later stages of development, and that’s the approach we’re taking as well. Since we don’t use procedurally generated landscapes or assets, creating each model, texture, and every corner of the locations takes a significant amount of time and resources. Of course, it’s all about working, working, and working.
To gauge the level of detail you can expect, look at the weapon, character, and vehicle models. The roughest part right now is the maps.

[h2]Q: What platforms will the game be on? Will it be available on mobile?[/h2]
A: PC only.

[h2]Q: Will the game be paid?[/h2]
A: Yes, it will be a paid game.
This way, we won’t have to rely on aggressive monetization methods like adding silly skins or ads. In my opinion, this is the better approach.

[h2]Q: Will there be microtransactions?[/h2]
A: To be safe, I'll say "Yes," but we're not heavily focusing on them. There definitely won’t be silly skins, “tactical” sportish guns, execution animations with bats or zombies, or anything like that. And of course, nothing that affects gameplay. We’d like to offer something rare and interesting, like unique camouflage or rare modifications of well-known weapons.

[h2]Q: When will it be possible to play? Is it possible to take part in closed testing?[/h2]
A: For an indie game, it’s crucial to start building a community as early as possible. While I’m here answering your questions and sharing our ideas, we’re also preparing the Pre-Alpha version. We’re aiming for a release around February-March 2025, and that’s when we’ll launch Patreon and Boosty, giving the first opportunity to get a key and play. We don’t want to ask for funding until we’ve made a decent trailer and a more polished version of the game.

[h2]Q: Tell us more about the class system[/h2]
A: The classic role distribution includes five classes: Assaulter (attacker), Heavy gunner (defender), Medic, Techman, and Recon. Each class will have three distinct specializations. For example, the Recon class can specialize as a Sniper focused on long-range combat, a Marksman for mid-range engagements, or a Saboteur specializing in close-quarters combat behind enemy lines. There’s also a unique sixth class — the Trooper. This is essentially your own custom character and class. You’ll be able to create a unique appearance and choose an even more narrowly focused specialization, allowing you to craft a soldier tailored precisely to your playstyle rather than a jack-of-all-trades.
In a few weeks, I plan to write a detailed post about the concept behind Entropia’s class system.

[h2]Q: Will there be weapon customization?[/h2]
A: Weapon customization has long been a standard in shooters, so of course, we’ll include it. Our focus is on functional customization (scopes, muzzle devices, flashlights, etc.) without delving too deeply into replacing weapon components.

[h2]Q: Will there be drivable vehicles?[/h2]
A: Drivable vehicles are undeniably awesome, and we’d love to implement them someday. We’ve even conceptualized a separate mode designed around vehicles. However, for now, our priority is to create gameplay that is enjoyable on its own, even without vehicles.
Later, when our small team will gain more experience and resources, we might revisit this idea.

[h2]Q: Will [insert weapon name] be in the game?[/h2]
A: We have a lot of weapons planned, but right now we’re focused on gameplay mechanics, which we believe are more important than adding new content at this stage.

[h2]Q: Can I support the game financially?[/h2]
A: Thank you for believing in us! However, we want to create a minimally playable version first before accepting any financial support. The Pre-Alpha release and crowdfunding launch are planned for February-March. For now, the development is funded by ad revenue from our YouTube channels (please understand and forgive, haha).

Thank you for your interest in Entropia!
If you have additional questions, suggestions, or just want to discuss the game, feel free to leave a comment in our Discord
Stay in touch!

notes.title: Welcome to Entropia
notes.content:
[b]It's a place to start![/b]

[previewyoutube=VLV5olzNCf0;full][/previewyoutube]

As the head of development, I’d like to introduce you to Entropia and share what’s coming soon.

Entropia is an original tactical first-person shooter featuring brutal battles in a fully destructible environment, a vast arsenal of weapons, customization, gadgets, and destruction!
Entropia is a game about people: an alternate history of the Modern Age, dozens of characters with their own personalities, relationships, traumas and ambitions. Just the way they are.
After all, Entropia is a game. Not a product. A game made by gamers without publishers, investors, or consultants of political correctness. Our responsibility is solely to the gamers—you and ourselves.

Entropia has just moved beyond the prototype stage, and we’re preparing a Pre-Alpha version set to release in early 2025.
Until then, we’re looking to build a community around the game, share development updates, and gather your feedback.

Join our Discord: [url=https://discord.com/invite/WGMzFPdTB7]https://discord.com/invite/WGMzFPdTB7[/url]
Website: [url=https://entropiathegame.com]https://entropiathegame.com[/url]

[i]— Maks Ulman and the June Folks team[/i]
